market_summary: Tech earnings are driving divergence in US large caps: Apple's Q4 beat gave a brief lift but the stock still slipped on the day as the print was largely priced in, while Tesla keeps grinding higher on persistent SpaceX-merger speculation and a cluster of analyst upgrades. Meta is under fresh UK regulatory pressure over AI content terms, adding to a rough month for the stock. In Singapore, the STI has pulled back 1.4% as DBS, OCBC and UOB trade down hard (heavy volume) ahead of Q3 results due Nov 4-6, a binary setup that could go either way. Overall US indices (SPY/QQQ) are soft from highs, reflecting broader risk-off tone even as mega-cap earnings season delivers mixed signals.

picks.thesis: Three separate sell-side upgrades in the last 10 days (Barclays, CLSA, BNP Paribas) have accompanied an 9% 1-month rally, and both Tesla and SpaceX have now formed independent board committees to formally explore a merger. This is a concrete process step (not just rumor), and speculation of this magnitude tends to keep a bid under the stock until there's clarity one way or the other. Price is already above both 50- and 200-day MAs, confirming the momentum shift.
picks.news: Tesla-SpaceX merger talks continue: both companies formed special committees of independent directors to explore a deal as of Nov 2, 2026; Barclays sees a possible announcement by year-end. Multiple brokers upgraded the stock Oct 22-26.
picks.risks: If the committees conclude there's no viable deal, or if talks drag on for months without progress, the speculative premium could unwind quickly. Valuation is already rich (45% annualized vol, beta 1.8), so any disappointment could trigger an outsized pullback.

picks.thesis: UK's CMA opened a formal competition investigation (Oct 30) into Meta's AI content-licensing terms for publishers, forcing Meta to pause a planned Nov 20 rollout. This adds a concrete regulatory overhang right as the stock is already down almost 17% in a month and 22% off its 52-week high, with price trading well below both 50- and 200-day MAs. Regulatory delays to AI monetization plans are a tangible negative catalyst, not just sentiment.
picks.news: UK CMA opened a competition investigation into Meta's AI content terms for publishers on Oct 30, 2026; Meta paused the Nov 20 implementation as a result.
picks.risks: Analyst consensus still implies ~40% upside and the stock has already sold off sharply, so a lot of bad news may be priced in; a quick resolution or earnings beat could spark a sharp reversal higher.

picks.thesis: DBS has pulled back 7% in a month on elevated volume (2.2x normal) purely ahead of its Nov 5 earnings release, with no company-specific negative news reported. Analyst consensus remains constructive (10 buy/6 hold/1 sell, ~10.5% implied upside), and the stock is still up 33% over the past year and trading above its 200-day MA, suggesting the recent drop is more sector-wide de-risking than a fundamental deterioration.
picks.news: Singapore banks fall ahead of Q3 earnings; DBS reports Nov 5, OCBC Nov 6, UOB mid-November, amid a 1.4% STI pullback (Nov 2, 2026).
picks.risks: This is a binary, earnings-driven trade: a Q3 miss or soft NIM guidance (rates backdrop) could extend the decline rather than reverse it. Typical results-day move is only ~1.9%, so the thesis plays out gradually, not immediately.

picks.thesis: Alphabet has sharply underperformed peers, down almost 19% in a month and nearly 31% off its 52-week high, with price well below both 50- and 200-day MAs. A sell-side downgrade (Citizens, Market Outperform to Market Perform, Oct 29) adds to the negative momentum, and there's no fresh positive catalyst in the available news to counter the trend.
picks.news: Citizens downgraded Alphabet from Market Outperform to Market Perform on Oct 29, 2026, after the stock had already fallen roughly 14% since.
picks.risks: The stock is already deeply oversold and the broad analyst base still models ~46% upside to target, so this could easily be a bottoming process rather than further downside; a bounce on any AI/ad-revenue news could quickly invalidate the short.
